claim: FGF21 analogues are in clinical development for type 2 diabetes and nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) treatment.
source: Analogues of the hepatokine fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21) are in clinical development for type 2 diabetes and nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) treatment.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Sanyal et al., 2019; Harrison et al., 2021).

claim: APOE*3-Leiden.CETP mice are a well-established model for human-like metabolic diseases.
source: Here, we aimed to unveil the mechanisms underlying the protective effects of FGF21 on NASH using APOE*3-Leiden.CETP mice, a well-established model for human-like metabolic diseases.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations (Morrison et al., 2015; Liang et al., 2014).

claim: FGF21 prevented hepatic lipotoxicity in APOE*3-Leiden.CETP mice fed a high-fat high-cholesterol diet.
source: FGF21 prevented hepatic lipotoxicity, accompanied by activation of thermogenic tissues and attenuation of adipose tissue inflammation, improvement of hyperglycemia and hypertriglyceridemia, and upregulation of hepatic programs involved in fatty acid oxidation and cholesterol removal.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing reduced liver lipid accumulation and improved metabolic parameters.

claim: FGF21 activates thermogenic tissues in APOE*3-Leiden.CETP mice.
source: FGF21 prevented hepatic lipotoxicity, accompanied by activation of thermogenic tissues and attenuation of adipose tissue inflammation, improvement of hyperglycemia and hypertriglyceridemia, and upregulation of hepatic programs involved in fatty acid oxidation and cholesterol removal.
evidence: This is supported by data showing increased UCP-1 expression in BAT and sWAT (Figure 2A, B).

claim: FGF21 attenuates adipose tissue inflammation in APOE*3-Leiden.CETP mice fed a high-fat high-cholesterol diet.
source: FGF21 prevented hepatic lipotoxicity, accompanied by activation of thermogenic tissues and attenuation of adipose tissue inflammation, improvement of hyperglycemia and hypertriglyceridemia, and upregulation of hepatic programs involved in fatty acid oxidation and cholesterol removal.
evidence: This is supported by data showing reduced crown-like structures and decreased expression of pro-inflammatory markers in gWAT (Figure 2C, D).

claim: FGF21 improves hyperglycemia in APOE*3-Leiden.CETP mice fed a high-fat high-cholesterol diet.
source: FGF21 prevented hepatic lipotoxicity, accompanied by activation of thermogenic tissues and attenuation of adipose tissue inflammation, improvement of hyperglycemia and hypertriglyceridemia, and upregulation of hepatic programs involved in fatty acid oxidation and cholesterol removal.
evidence: This is supported by data showing normalized fasting plasma glucose and improved glucose tolerance (Figure 3A, B).

claim: FGF21 improves hypertriglyceridemia in APOE*3-Leiden.CETP mice fed a high-fat high-cholesterol diet.
source: FGF21 prevented hepatic lipotoxicity, accompanied by activation of thermogenic tissues and attenuation of adipose tissue inflammation, improvement of hyperglycemia and hypertriglyceridemia, and upregulation of hepatic programs involved in fatty acid oxidation and cholesterol removal.
evidence: This is supported by data showing reduced fasting plasma triglyceride levels (Figure 3D).

claim: FGF21 upregulates hepatic programs involved in fatty acid oxidation.
source: FGF21 prevented hepatic lipotoxicity, accompanied by activation of thermogenic tissues and attenuation of adipose tissue inflammation, improvement of hyperglycemia and hypertriglyceridemia, and upregulation of hepatic programs involved in fatty acid oxidation and cholesterol removal.
evidence: This is supported by data showing increased expression of Cpt1a, Ppara, and Pgc1a (Figure 5B).

claim: FGF21 upregulates hepatic programs involved in cholesterol removal.
source: FGF21 prevented hepatic lipotoxicity, accompanied by activation of thermogenic tissues and attenuation of adipose tissue inflammation, improvement of hyperglycemia and hypertriglyceridemia, and upregulation of hepatic programs involved in fatty acid oxidation and cholesterol removal.
evidence: This is supported by data showing increased expression of Abcg5 and Cyp7a1 (Figure 5C, D).

claim: FGF21 inhibits hepatic inflammation by reducing Kupffer cell activation.
source: Furthermore, FGF21 inhibited hepatic inflammation, as evidenced by reduced Kupffer cell (KC) activation, diminished monocyte infiltration, and lowered accumulation of monocyte-derived macrophages.

claim: FGF21 diminishes monocyte infiltration in the liver.
source: Furthermore, FGF21 inhibited hepatic inflammation, as evidenced by reduced Kupffer cell (KC) activation, diminished monocyte infiltration, and lowered accumulation of monocyte-derived macrophages.

claim: FGF21 lowers the accumulation of monocyte-derived macrophages in the liver.
source: Furthermore, FGF21 inhibited hepatic inflammation, as evidenced by reduced Kupffer cell (KC) activation, diminished monocyte infiltration, and lowered accumulation of monocyte-derived macrophages.

claim: FGF21 decreases lipid-associated macrophages in the liver.
source: Moreover, FGF21 decreased lipid- and scar-associated macrophages, which correlated with less hepatic fibrosis as demonstrated by reduced collagen accumulation.
evidence: This is supported by flow cytometry data showing reduced CD36hi ResKCs and CD36hi MoKCs (Figure 6B, C).

claim: FGF21 decreases scar-associated macrophages in the liver.
source: Moreover, FGF21 decreased lipid- and scar-associated macrophages, which correlated with less hepatic fibrosis as demonstrated by reduced collagen accumulation.

claim: FGF21 reduces hepatic fibrosis as demonstrated by reduced collagen accumulation.
source: Moreover, FGF21 decreased lipid- and scar-associated macrophages, which correlated with less hepatic fibrosis as demonstrated by reduced collagen accumulation.
evidence: This is supported by data showing reduced Picrosirius Red staining, hydroxyproline content, and COL1A1 expression (Figure 4D, E, Figure 6D).

claim: Hepatic FGF21 overexpression limits hepatic lipotoxicity, inflammation, and fibrogenesis.
source: Collectively, hepatic FGF21 overexpression limits hepatic lipotoxicity, inflammation, and fibrogenesis.
evidence: This is a summary statement supported by multiple experimental findings throughout the study.

claim: FGF21 blocks hepatic lipid influx through endocrine signaling.
source: Mechanistically, FGF21 blocks hepatic lipid influx and accumulation through combined endocrine and autocrine signaling, respectively, which prevents KC activation and lowers the presence of lipid- and scar-associated macrophages to inhibit fibrogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from data showing activation of thermogenic tissues and reduced adipose tissue inflammation, which would reduce lipid overflow to the liver.

claim: FGF21 blocks hepatic lipid accumulation through autocrine signaling.
source: Mechanistically, FGF21 blocks hepatic lipid influx and accumulation through combined endocrine and autocrine signaling, respectively, which prevents KC activation and lowers the presence of lipid- and scar-associated macrophages to inhibit fibrogenesis.

claim: FGF21 prevents KC activation by blocking hepatic lipid influx and accumulation.
source: Mechanistically, FGF21 blocks hepatic lipid influx and accumulation through combined endocrine and autocrine signaling, respectively, which prevents KC activation and lowers the presence of lipid- and scar-associated macrophages to inhibit fibrogenesis.

claim: FGF21 lowers the presence of lipid- and scar-associated macrophages to inhibit fibrogenesis.
source: Mechanistically, FGF21 blocks hepatic lipid influx and accumulation through combined endocrine and autocrine signaling, respectively, which prevents KC activation and lowers the presence of lipid- and scar-associated macrophages to inhibit fibrogenesis.

claim: Adipose tissue dysfunction and lipid spillover leads to hepatic lipotoxicity, and thereby the initiation of NASH.
